thread:
Alyssa (CSM): Morning — posting the weekly health snapshot for Luxon private deployment (US/EU regions). Quick bullets: usage steady, small uptick in 400s from eu-central, intermittent KMS timeouts in us-west-2 last night.

Theo (SRE): Thanks. Can you paste the region-by-region uptime numbers?

Alyssa (CSM): Sure — last 7d rolling: us-west-2 99.92% (one 14m window), us-east-1 99.99%, eu-central-1 99.80 (three brief drops), ap-southeast-1 100%.

Priya (AE): Noted on the eu-central dips — customer mentioned increased token volume after feature launch. Any error rates by endpoint?

Sam (Solutions Eng): Endpoint error breakup (7d avg): generation API 0.6% errors, embeddings 0.1%, auth failures ~0.02%. The 400 spikes in eu-central are mostly 429/500 mix.

Theo (SRE): KMS alerts showed timeouts ~ 2026-03-18 02:14-02:28 UTC for us-west-2. KMS-monitor-bot flagged latency to HSM gateway ~> 2.1s for key unwrap ops. We retried and fell back to cached DEKs, but there were a few requests that hit the timeout threshold.

kms-monitor-bot: [alert] Luxon-us-west-2: KMS unwrap latency p95=2.11s, error-rate=0.9% (window=15m). Links: https://internal.ops/alerts/AL-7891

Alyssa (CSM): Customer message: "saw a handful of failed requests around 02:15 UTC, impacted our inference pipeline for ~10m". They attached logs — asked for root cause.

Sam (Solutions Eng): I pulled sample logs. Here's the relevant trace snippet from the private runtime proxy: 

```
2026-03-18T02:15:08Z proxy-1 luxon: request-id=afe12c key-unwrap start
2026-03-18T02:15:10Z kms-proxy: unwrap failed: timeout after 2000ms
2026-03-18T02:15:10Z proxy-1 luxon: fallback to DEK cache hit
2026-03-18T02:15:12Z proxy-1 luxon: request completed with 500 for user request 0x9b
```

Theo (SRE): Good capture. Root cause appears transient KMS reverse-proxy overload. On-call increased concurrency for background rotations earlier that hour. I throttled rotation jobs and bumped HSM connection pool from 20 -> 40 as a short-term mitigation.

Priya (AE): Any customer impact metrics we should share for renewal thread? They want to know SLA hit risk.

Alyssa (CSM): Impact: 12 failed requests (0.003% of weekly volume), latency tail for impacted requests +600ms. No sustained SLA breach. I'll summarize as "brief transient KMS latency spike causing a small number of retries; mitigated and monitoring."

Sam (Solutions Eng): Recommendation for next week: 1) add circuit-breaker to KMS calls in runtime to fail fast and use cached keys more aggressively, 2) schedule KMS-heavy background jobs off-peak, 3) 24h monitoring rule for p95 unwrap latency >1.5s.

Theo (SRE): I'll open an infra ticket to add the monitoring rule and make rotation jobs aware of system load: INFRA-1247. Also will run a load repro on staging to validate new pool sizing.

kms-monitor-bot: [note] Incident mitigated at 2026-03-18T02:40:00Z; follow-up ticket INFRA-1247 created.

Alyssa (CSM): Great — I'll send the one-paragraph customer note and schedule a short enablement call to walk through retry logic and caching knobs. Priya, looping you to coordinate the call with account stakeholders.

Priya (AE): Happy to schedule — propose Wednesday 14:00 CET. I'll DM the calendar invite.

Alyssa (CSM): Thanks team. Anything else for this week's health check?

Sam (Solutions Eng): One more: request to validate KMS key rotation window with customer's security team. I'll ask for their rotation cadence and share recommended timing.

Alyssa (CSM): Perfect. Closing notes: no renewal risk flagged; recommended follow-ups logged (monitoring + infra ticket + customer call). :white_check_mark:

Theo (SRE): 👍

Priya (AE): :thumbsup:
